The VitePress docs site (`docs/`, `@pantoken/docs`) has two locales: `root` (English, `/…`) and
`hu` (Magyar, `/hu/…`), a symmetric prefix swap including `/api/` ↔ `/hu/api/`.

**Translation layer = `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` (`LocaleMeta`) holds ALL
localizable UI strings: nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, plus (added Jul 2026) `themeSelector`
(the custom palette selector's button + palette labels — `Canvas` stays as-is per brand rules),
`chrome` (VitePress default-theme labels: outline, docFooter, dark/light switch, sidebarMenu,
returnToTop, langMenu, lastUpdated, notFound), and `search` (local-search UI). `config.ts` expands
these into per-locale `themeConfig` (VitePress deep-merges it recursively over the global
themeConfig via `stackView`, so per-locale `outline.label` keeps the global `outline.level`).
Search translations are the exception — they live in the GLOBAL `themeConfig.search.options.locales`
keyed by locale index, because the local-search index reads the root themeConfig. `ThemeSelector.vue`
reads its strings at runtime via `useData().theme.value.themeSelector` (falls back to
`THEME_SELECTOR_DEFAULTS` in theme.ts). When English UI is added, port it here, not inline.

**Adapter split.** Guides (`docs/scripts/translate-guides.ts`, hand-written prose) use the
`claude-code` adapter (`docs:guides:locales:claude`) for real translation. The generated API tree
(`docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`, TypeDoc + CSS reference) uses the default `glossary` adapter
(`docs:api:locales`) — deterministic term-swap, well-suited to structural reference content
(headings like Parameters/Returns/Példák; identifiers and code stay as-is). Don't run `:claude` over
the whole API tree: the content-hash `i18n-cache/` was fully stale as of this work (0/598 hits), so
it means ~598 sequential `claude -p` calls (hours). `check-locale-parity.ts` gates the build and now

**i18nRouting audit (VitePress 2.0.0-alpha.18 / PR #5239):** we deliberately do NOT set a custom
`i18nRouting` function. Our symmetric prefix structure is exactly what VitePress's default handles —
its nav switchers use `useLangs({ correspondingLink: true })` (switch maps to the corresponding
page) and `cleanUrls: true` yields clean links. See the comment near `locales:` in config.ts. See

# Docs site + `vitepress-plugin-llms` findings

## 1. Where the plugin is configured

**File:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/.vitepress/config.ts`

The plugin is imported at line 6 (`import llmstxt from "vitepress-plugin-llms";`) and registered inside the Vite plugins array (`vite.plugins`) at lines 363–369. The **full options passed are just two**:

```ts
vite: {
  plugins: [
    orchestrator,
    llmstxt({
      title: "pantoken",
      description,
    }) as never,
  ],
  ...
}
```

where `description` (line 235–236) is:
```ts
const description =
  "Instructure design tokens and icons, reshaped for every platform and framework.";
```

That's the entire config. **No `workDir`, `ignoreFiles`, `ignoreFilesPerOutput`, `domain`, `customLLMsTxtTemplate`, `generateLLMsFullTxt`, `exclude*`, or `experimental.depth` is set** — everything else runs at the plugin defaults. Related (not plugin config, but the surfacing of its output): a nav social link points at `${base}llms.txt` (lines 435–440).

There is **no `srcDir` or `srcExclude`** set in the VitePress config, so VitePress's source root is `docs/` and the plugin's `workDir` defaults to that whole tree — meaning it processes **both** `docs/hu/**` and the generated `docs/api/**` alongside the English guides, producing a single combined `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` with no per-locale separation.
